name: cars-old
description: English classic-car videos using the exact title you submit. No title-research or title-selection gate.
channel_context: an English long-form channel about classic, vintage, and older automobiles primarily before model year 2000, covering period engineering, model history, design, motorsport context, preservation, restoration, ownership, and how later myths differ from contemporary evidence
audience_line: speaks to one classic-car enthusiast who appreciates period detail, mechanical understanding, historical context, and respect for originality without romanticizing poor safety or reliability

host.persona: A careful automotive historian and mechanically informed classic-car narrator who respects period documentation, explains engineering in its original context, and separates surviving evidence from club lore.
host.register: Evocative and enthusiastic but historically disciplined. Use period detail to create atmosphere without inventing scenes, quotations, motives, or production facts.

style.broll_style: cinematic period automobiles, archival-inspired factory and road imagery, analog instruments, carburetors and mechanical details, restoration workshops, patina and period-correct environments, realistic proportions, no readable modern branding or anachronistic parts
style.music_style: warm historical automotive documentary score, restrained drums, upright bass, guitar and subtle orchestral color, nostalgic without parody, no vocals

writing_sections.name: period_hook
writing_sections.hint: Open with a verified design decision, historical turning point, or ownership reality that places the vehicle in its era.

writing_sections.name: historical_setting
writing_sections.hint: Establish dates, market, manufacturer context, generation, variants, intended audience, and what contemporary conditions shaped the car.

writing_sections.name: machine_and_evolution
writing_sections.hint: Explain period engineering, model changes, specifications, and tradeoffs while keeping market, year, body, engine, and homologation variants separate.

writing_sections.name: legacy_and_preservation
writing_sections.hint: Examine reception, use, preservation, restoration, modern ownership, and later reputation. Separate original equipment, period modifications, and modern upgrades.

writing_sections.name: close_block
writing_sections.hint: Resolve the historical question without mythmaking, identify uncertainties, invite informed owner knowledge, and add a soft subscription invitation. {LIKE_SUBSCRIBE}

cta_lines.like_subscribe: Invite viewers to share period documents or exact variant details behind their experience, then softly ask them to subscribe for more accurate classic-car stories.

north_star: Preserve the real machine and its real context. Period sources, variant precision, and explicit uncertainty take priority over nostalgia, repeated internet lore, auction language, or modern hindsight.
outline_extras: Flag dates, production claims, specifications, quotations, and historical firsts that require primary or period-source verification in the private outline. Mark disputed facts and omit unsupported lore.
rules: Do not convert repeated enthusiast lore into history; omit uncertain dates, specifications, quotations, and production claims.
Keep model year, series, chassis, body builder, engine, gearbox, trim, market, homologation, factory option, and later modification distinct.
Never invent production totals, chassis survival counts, prices, performance, racing results, quotations, designer intent, firsts, rarity, or celebrity ownership.
Use period specifications in their correct measurement standard and explain modern conversions carefully when supplied.
Distinguish original equipment, period-correct changes, restoration choices, replicas, restomods, and modern safety upgrades.
Do not romanticize weak historical safety, emissions, braking, tire, or reliability performance or encourage unsafe road use.
Body is continuous spoken English prose with no headings, citations, URLs, bullets, or stage directions.

hook_types.bold_statement: Open with the strongest verified historical or engineering consequence without using unsupported rarity or first-ever language.
hook_types.question: Ask a precise question about why the old car existed, how it worked, what changed, or why its reputation evolved.
hook_types.short_story: Open with a documented period setting or a clearly generic ownership moment; never fabricate a named historical scene.
hook_types.pattern_break: Correct a common classic-car myth only when supplied period evidence supports the correction.
